name: Hall Sharp Three-Repair Growth Example
definition: Let $K=C_H$ be Hall's 299-concept obstruction with compatible repairs $a=183$, $b=315$, and $d=1836$. On a new coordinate $p$, put $H=((K\cup\{b\})\times\{0\})\cup((K\cup\{a\})\times\{1\})$, add $c=(d,0)$ to obtain $S$, and then form the opposite-layer lift $X=((S\cup\{(d,1)\})\times\{0\})\cup((S\cup\{(b,1)\})\times\{1\})$ on a second coordinate $q$.
parameters: $H$ has 600 concepts, $S$ has 601, and $X$ has 1,204. The obstruction-preserving corner deletion removes the second-layer copy of $c$ and leaves a terminal 1,203-concept Hall facet assembly.
properties: $\mathcal R(H)=\{(a,0),(b,1)\}$ while $\mathcal R(S)=\{(a,0),(b,1),(d,1)\}$, so the new adjacent repair attains both repair-growth bounds. Every old coordinate of $S$ occurs in 165 minimal forbidden traces and $p$ occurs in three, so $S$ has no successful layer set. In $X$, $q$ is the unique successful layer and recovers the cornered seed $S$. Deleting the specified corner makes both $p$ and $q$ balanced and recovers Hall on the two-layer set; the resulting rows form a terminal signed-facet partition.
